This binding leads to the activation of phospholipase C, which catalyzes the hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) into diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3). DAG activates protein kinase C, while IP3 releases calcium from intracellular stores, leading to muscle contraction. By blocking muscarinic receptors, ipratropium bromide prevents this response, resulting in bronchodilation.
